items.reviewNote: L’Être éternel refers to the divine being, a noun rather than copular or auxiliary être. The earlier Chapter I plural general-entities plan and singular living-being plan were inspected. Share the general-entities meaning and reconcile the narrower singular wording; its new-sense route must be corrected to a proper French noun lemma before import; the published être verb cannot own this noun. Add a deity-context bank on general being, without claiming a material living creature or copying verb mastery. Être/endroit/moment/mouvement are masculine singular, and the general existence clue selects être.

Autant vaudrait ne pas être means not existing, rather than linking a subject to an attribute or being present somewhere. The global existential être sense was inspected, with its impersonal examples. This absolute bank shares existence; before activation impact-review the family to broaden the impersonal wording transparently without resetting unchanged existential mastery or inventing an infinitive-only sense.

Éternel modifies the divine being within the giant’s conception. No proper French published or earlier eternal adjective family exists. The bank tests endless duration and does not assert the truth of a theology; all masculine singular alternatives fit the predicate.

Manifester makes divine skill and power evident through creatures; it is not taking part in a political demonstration. No published or earlier French manifester family exists. The four infinitives fit the direct object cette puissance, while making evident contrasts with hiding, denying and forgetting.

The Creator’s adresse is inventive skill, not a postal location or solely manual microscope dexterity. The earlier V skill plan and its three banks were inspected; this bank augments that same planned noun sense for the theological figure. Adresse/maladresse/chance/force are feminine singular; habileté selects adresse without a creative-only duplicate sense.

Both source uses attribute effective creative power to the eternal being. The existing noun power family and its three political-power banks were read; the general force meaning applies, with these new contextual questions rather than an institution-only bank. All four nouns are feminine singular after la. The later potentiality use receives a distinct proposed meaning under the same noun lemma.

The Peripatetic defines a capacity of the soul to be what it is. This technical potentiality differs from the active power praised in units 169 and 208; prepare it on the existing proper French noun lemma. Puissance/présence/apparence/mémoire are feminine singular and fit une; potential capacity selects puissance. The text’s Aristotelian attribution is reported, not independently endorsed as an accurate quotation.

Goûter des joies figuratively means experiencing pleasure, not tasting food. No published or earlier proper French goûter family exists. Each infinitive fits les, and the pleasure clue selects goûter without requiring a physical taste sensation.

The giant assumes pure joys for the tiny people; the later reply challenges that assumption. The canonical French joie noun sense was compared with the older joy gloss; this is plural happy feeling, not a number-only meaning. Joies/peines/craintes/hontes are feminine plural and fit leurs; happiness alone selects joies.

Pures describes the speaker’s imagined unmixed joys, not literal clean water or a proved moral innocence. The existing adjective definition includes unsoiled/unmixed but specifies water. Record an explicit shared-family impact dependency to broaden contextual wording before activation, preserving unchanged purity mastery rather than inventing an abstract-only duplicate; all choices match feminine plural joies.

Paraissant tout esprit describes an appearance inferred from little matter. The global seem and appear families were inspected; preserve the previously chosen proper seem sense. Each participle takes the infinitive n’être; seeming differs from believing, claiming or affirming. No truth of an immaterial nature is asserted.

The Cartesian’s âme est un esprit pur and the giant’s question about esprit concern an immaterial thinking entity. The global esprit family includes immaterial beings independently of group ethos and intellectual faculty. Add this philosophical context to the existing immaterial-being meaning, not a ghost-only interpretation or a philosopher-only duplicate. Esprit/corps/organe/muscle are masculine singular and fit un.

The giant likens the tiny people’s life to that of immaterial spirits. Existing plural questions invoke folklore, so this source-specific philosophical bank augments the same global immaterial-being sense. All four choices are masculine plural. The literal mind uses and group ethos are excluded, and no plural-only sense or new mastery copied from singular is invented.

All five standalone tous uses resume an entire plural group. The proper lem_fr_tout_pronoun owns the published all-of-them sense, currently worded for feminine toutes; broaden that gender-specific wording only after shared-family impact review. Do not attach the pronoun to a determiner lemma or invent a masculine-only sense. The four plural pronouns are grammatical, with no exception selecting tous.

The philosophers shake their heads in response to the claim of happiness. The following admission supports dissent, but the lexical verb denotes shaking rather than a gesture-only sense. No published or earlier secouer family exists; the anatomical tête keeps its already planned noun meaning and no separate idiom is invented.

Plus franc characterizes the philosopher’s open admission. The global franc adjective lemma has a freedom/Frankish gloss, while a separate noun lemma denotes currency; neither owns this honest meaning. Prepare sincerity under the proper existing French adjective lemma, preserving those other meanings. Each masculine singular predicate fits il est; candid expression selects franc.

The frank philosopher openly acknowledges the poor state of humanity. The global avouer admit sense already covers acknowledging what one might conceal; no confession of a personal crime is inferred. Add the past-historic surface and all three contextual bands to that same verb sense without a tense-only duplicate.

The conditional excludes a small number of inhabitants from the unfavorable judgment about the rest. No global or earlier excepter family exists. All four third-person predicates fit the direct object ce petit groupe; exclusion rather than inclusion, counting or description selects excepte. The people are not literally expelled from a place.

Both petit nombre phrases describe a few inhabitants or sages, not their physical stature. The global small/young adjective family was read; before activation impact-review its scope wording to include numerical smallness. Retain unchanged smallness mastery and avoid a quantity-only duplicate. All four masculine singular adjectives fit nombre, with few in quantity selecting petit.

Fort peu considérés means little esteemed, not merely seldom observed visually. The global considérer verb family has attentive looking and mental examination but lacks social regard. Prepare esteem under that proper existing French verb lemma; the source’s low degree is carried by peu/fort rather than reversing the lexical meaning. All four participles match masculine plural inhabitants.

The impersonal clause states that fewer than a hundredth of the people remain after ten years. The global proper rester family includes left-over/subsisting, distinct from the exact surface’s staying-in-a-place bank and from the remainder noun. Prepare this source bank on the existing left-over meaning, preserving other mastery. All four impersonal third-person singular predicates are grammatical with a postverbal une petite partie; subsistence rather than arrival, return or disappearance selects reste.

The eternal being is personified as taking pleasure in revealing ingenuity and power. The exact VI plaire bank and all three bands were read and reused unchanged. The four pronominal prefixes fit an infinitive; pleasure differs from refusal, reluctant acceptance and limitation. No isolated plu, est or s’ encounter is added.

The philosophers answer and speak simultaneously. The Chapter V full-span bank was read in all three bands and reused unchanged; neither repeated occasions nor one-after-another applies. The new exhaustive VII spans suppress component à/la/fois identities without copying mastery.

The second speaker adds that he too does not understand Greek. The earlier IV bank was read and retained unchanged in all three bands. It adds a second negation rather than expressing increased degree, immediacy or indefinite duration; plus does not receive a separate quantity encounter here.

The philosopher adds that the remote rulers, rather than the soldiers alone, deserve punishment. The VI full-span bank and its published component identity were inspected and reused unchanged. This is an additional argument, not spatial elsewhere; final import must retain the published meaning with no duplicate component mastery.

Nulle part denies any location where the traveler has found true happiness. The four full phrases fit the negated seeing construction; lack of a place differs from another place, every place or an unspecified place. Part is neither a portion noun nor the verb departing in this span.

The frank philosopher candidly admits widespread folly and unhappiness. The earlier VII expression draft has no approved questions; its sincerity disposition was checked, then these three bands were authored. All adverbial choices fit le dit, while honesty rather than reluctance, secrecy or insincerity selects the phrase. Bonne is not a maid and foi is not a promised word.

The three impersonal clauses name what the quarrel concerns, including negation of the claimed motive. The global agir family already has sns_zola_s_agir_concern, distinct from accomplishing an action. Prepare this full fused pronominal surface on that existing meaning, not a second expression sense. The middle alternatives are syntactically possible with de ce tas, while the stated subject of the dispute selects s’agit. Final import must bridge the whole span and suppress s’/agit duplicate encounters.

Académie 7 user explicitly records absolute en user for acting in a particular manner. The global proper user verb has only wear-down, so prepare this distinct behaving meaning under lem_fr_user_verb. This is how humans wage war, not deterioration by rubbing. All middle predicates are grammatical; behavior rather than wearing an object, using a tool or purchasing selects the whole construction. No anaphoric en encounter is duplicated.

The philosopher presents warfare as having persisted beyond remembered beginnings. The bank tests the phrase’s temporal meaning, not a factual date of the first war. All four temporal phrases fit the verb; remote unremembered antiquity selects the target. The noun temps and adjective immémorial remain inside the full-span identity.

The philosophers agree on two or three understood points, contrasting their many disputes. The full agreeing predicate is prepared, excluding generic de and musical accord. Each alternative fits ils sont; shared opinion rather than disagreement, uncertainty or urgency selects agreement. Published d’accord component meanings require one canonical full-span route before import.

Point du tout and rien du tout reinforce a complete negation, concerning understanding and action respectively. They are not the quantity pronoun tout standing for everything. All adverbs fit the negative completion while absolute exclusion alone selects du tout; each complete source span is retained to suppress duplicate component mastery.

The Peripatetic says the proposition aloud. Haut is not spatial elevation, and tout intensifies the established vocal expression. All four manner phrases fit les dit; audibility rather than silence, secrecy or an inward thought selects tout haut. Before import reconcile any existing haut loud meaning into one whole-span route rather than duplicate word and phrase encounters.

The giant contrasts what is outside the philosophers with their interior soul and thinking. This figurative inward domain retains the inside/outside opposition; it does not mean bodily location alone. All four locative phrases fit se trouve. The whole locution is prepared so en is not incorrectly treated as a partitive pronoun.

The Cartesian claim says the soul must learn everything again; tout remains the pronoun everything outside de nouveau. No adjective meaning new modifies an object here. All temporal phrases fit apprend; repetition rather than first occurrence, indefinite duration or anticipation selects the target.

Académie 1762 regarder explicitly gives regarder quelqu’un de haut en bas for showing contempt or disdain. The source’s tiny cleric claims universal knowledge and human primacy before giants; this contextual application is an editorial inference supported by the conventional idiom, rather than a mere vertical survey. The earlier unresolved gaze draft was inspected. All four adverbial phrases fit regarde; contempt rather than respect, curiosity or indifference selects the whole locution.

The Sirian politely requests an account of the sages’ activities. This source formula is an entreaty, not the response to thanks that identical words can express elsewhere. Each first-person clause fits the quotation; polite requesting rather than prohibition, reproach or congratulation selects it. Je/vous/en/prie components stay within this specific formula.

The philosophers give the lunar distance as a rounded quantity. The question tests rounding and does not endorse a modern astronomical measurement. Each manner phrase fits exprimée; round approximation rather than exactness, absence of a number or ordering selects the target. Nominal rond is not physical circularity here.

Micromégas takes up the reported attributes and asks for the underlying nature of matter. The formula advances the exchange, not a claim of good quality, proficiency or willingness. All complete interjections fit the quotation. Published bien discourse meanings must be reconciled into a full formula before import so one occurrence does not generate two encounters.

Both occurrences introduce an alternative metaphor for soul and body. Every occurrence of ou bien in this unit is indexed, including the second one. Bien does not express knowledge quality or certainty here. All connectors fit the two clauses, while alternatives rather than succession, consequence or opposition select ou bien.

The historical à l’heure que clause states that the warfare is occurring as the philosopher speaks. The temporal relative construction is prepared in full rather than assigning que an unrelated object-relative bank. The first-person parle form works with all four connective alternatives; contemporaneity rather than before, after or cause selects the phrase.

The Malebranchist claims that God acts without his involvement. This is absence of the subordinate action, not the bare sans question under shared repair. The first-person mêle form fits all four conjunctions, with absence versus concession, cause and purpose selecting sans que. The philosophical claim stays attributed to the speaker.

The Lockean reports thinking only in connection with his sensory experiences. Occasion names a circumstance giving rise to thinking, not a festive celebration. All prepositional phrases fit ces expériences, while the asserted occasion rather than obstacle, temporal precedence or replacement selects the target. No historical proof of a theory is claimed.

The giant names tiny people who nevertheless possess vast pride. This substantivized masculine plural phrase differs from the singular abstract domain l’infiniment petit reviewed in VI. All four complete noun phrases are masculine plural and fit appelle. The full span prevents an isolated article plus an unrelated adjective from becoming duplicated vocabulary identities. The earlier V substantive petits plan and all three banks were read: they denote the same tiny beings. Before import, correct that nominal ownership away from the adjective lemma, share the planned noun meaning, and reconcile the two complete spans without a new meaning or duplicate mastery.

Un peu modifies fâché with slight degree rather than naming one object. All four adverbial phrases fit the unchanged masculine singular adjective; low positive intensity rather than high intensity, completeness or zero selects the target. Prepare the full degree phrase so the un component is not falsely routed as an indefinite article encounter.

reviewBasis: Full source thought units, independently written meaning clues, every middle alternative, noun number and agreement, distinct meanings and explicit ownership dependencies were individually inspected. Structural checks verify revision and coverage, never editorial approval.
